newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, seen flat on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, seen flat on Thursday.

text.p: Polish shares on Wednesday extended Tuesday's fall but analysts said the market might have put the bulk of its profit-taking correction behind it after surging since mid-December on heightened foreign demand.

All the bourse's banks fell on Wednesday, with many extending losses after the central bank's Monday decision to raise mandatory reserves on zloty call and currency deposits, and analysts said some banks would fall again Thursday.
"Prices should remain around current levels but I wouldn't expect growth from that branch (banks)," said Krzysztof Olszewski, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 2.3 percent to 16,299.0 points and turnover eased 4.2 percent to 213 million zlotys ($70.9 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 68 to eight with 10 stocks flat.
Analysts said significant falls by some banks, such as Kredyt Bank which tumbled 8.1 percent, suggested that some banks would soon rebound.
Among big losing banks WBK fell six percent, PPABank 5.4 percent and BPH 4.8 percent.

Computer maker Optimus, the main market's biggest loser, fell 9.8 percent in profit-taking, extending Tuesday's fall after surging over 100 percent this month in part on good 1996 earnings which the firm says it might repeat this year.
Continuous trade turnover was at 36.2 million zlotys ($12.1 million) with 11 stocks down and six flat.

Mass privatisaton NFI units fell 2.6 percent to 150 zlotys ($50) in 29.3-million-zloty ($9.8 million) regular bourse trade and rose 0.3 percent to 148.5 zlotys ($49.50) in 28.5-million- zloty ($9.5 million) continuous trade.
